subject: Quantica sustained P99 latency spike — credit request & remediation timeline
messages:
From: Sienna Park <sienna.park@quantica.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hale <oliver.hale@quantica.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sustained P99 spike impacting inference pipelines — immediate support and credits requested

Logan,

We're seeing a sustained P99 latency spike across our production fleet starting ~2027-01-18 23:00 UTC that is causing timeouts and elevated error rates for our customer-facing flows. Error rate on /v1/generate increased from ~0.3% baseline to 4.8% during the window; several requests retried and a handful timed out. This has materially impacted two downstream features in our app and we have customers opening tickets.

Attached: short monitoring sample (attached as latency-sample.log) and a screenshot of the Grafana chart. We need:
- A clear immediate mitigation plan (routing/variant suggestions or capacity relief)
- A postmortem and a remediation timeline
- A calculation of SLA credits available to us and next steps to claim them

We are under contract with the standard SLA in section 4.2. I flagged this to our COO and they'll want an executive summary. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Sienna
Sienna Park
Director of Platform Engineering | Quantica AI
Attachments: latency-sample.log (text), grafana-trend-20270118.png (image)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sienna Park <sienna.park@quantica.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hale <oliver.hale@quantica.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sustained P99 spike impacting inference pipelines — immediate support and credits requested

Hi Sienna — thanks for the quick note and the evidence. I'm really sorry Quantica hit this. We have ops on it now and are treating this as a high-priority incident.

Immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Routed new traffic to a lower-latency model-variant in us-west while we triage the underlying kernel/packing regression.
- Autoscale policy forced an extra pool allocation to relieve queueing pressure; you should see reduced tail latency within the next 20–30 minutes.
- Ops is collecting full trace slices and will share a postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow.

For credits: we'll calculate the service credit per the SLA. I'll run the calc and propose a credit figure within 48 hours. If acceptable, we can process the credit as an invoice adjustment or a one-time refund — whatever your finance prefers.

Can we schedule an executive sync tomorrow 11:00 PT to walk through the remediation steps and credit calculation? I can bring Monica (Customer Success) and Ben (Finance lead) if helpful.

Again — apologies and we're on it.

— Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 12:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantica sustained P99 spike — proposed credit math + options

Team — forwarding Quantica's initial report. Ops handed me an early window and the SLA spreadsheet (attached). Preliminary numbers suggest Quantica experienced 9.6 hours of degraded service across the 48h window we care about, which maps to a ~6.8% service credit under our standard formula (see attached SLA calc).

Recommendation: offer two options to expedite resolution and retain the account:
1) Monetary credit: invoice adjustment equal to the calculated credit (~$35,400) applied to their Feb invoice.
2) Commercial relief: apply a 3‑month 20% discount on committed capacity in lieu of the credit (cap equal to $48k).

We typically cap one-off credits at $25k without exec sign-off — Quantica is a strategic midmarket account and their ARR is growing. Ask: Vivek, can you approve up to $50k for either of the above options? Also confirm whether finance should process as credit or refund. Ops to provide final postmortem by EOD Wed. Attaching draft calc and notes.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: quantica_sla_calc_QNT-4921.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 14:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quantica sustained P99 spike — proposed credit math + options

Monica — approve up to $40k credit as one-time invoice adjustment. Please keep final credit at or below the computed SLA amount if possible.

Requirements before we commit:
- Ops to confirm root cause and provide a remediation ETA (I want an engineer-level 48-hour remediation commitment).
- Offer the temporary routing to the variant and confirm any model-variant cost delta absorbed by Redwood for the initial 72 hours.
- Legal to confirm there are no contract amendments required for this credit.

Ben — flag finance for an invoice adj workflow and prepare a short approval note for accounting. Monica/Logan, once Quantica confirms acceptance we will cut the credit.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sienna Park <sienna.park@quantica.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hale <oliver.hale@quantica.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed credit and 48-hour remediation plan for Quantica (QNT-4921)

Sienna / Oliver — thanks again for the patience while we analyzed the incident. Below is the proposal from Redwood: 

Summary of findings (short): ops traced the degradation to an edge kernel scheduling regression that increased request queuing under sustained burst traffic. We have a code patch being validated and a controlled rollout plan.

Remediation & near-term mitigations:
- Immediate: traffic routed to the lower-latency model-variant (no config changes required on your side). This is live now and should reduce P99 within minutes.
- 48-hour remediation: we will deploy the fix to the canary ring within 12 hours, then a full rollout with rollback gating within 48 hours.
- Weekly ops sync: 30-minute standup for the next four weeks to review telemetry and validate regressions are resolved.

Commercial proposal:
- Calculated SLA credit: $35,400 (per attached SLA calc spreadsheet) — applied as an invoice adjustment to your Feb invoice.
- Executive-approved cap: Vivek approved up to $40,000; this figure is within that limit.
- Optional alternative: 3-month 20% committed-capacity discount (we can provide a side-by-side comparison if you'd like).

Next steps we need from Quantica: please confirm acceptance of the invoice adjustment approach or request the discount alternative. Once accepted, Ben will coordinate with your finance lead and we will issue the credit. I've attached the SLA calc and a short remediation timeline for your legal/finance review.

If it helps, we can put the credit proposal into DocuSign for acceptance.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: quantica_sla_calc_QNT-4921.xlsx, remediation-timeline-20270120.pdf
From: Sienna Park <sienna.park@quantica.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hale <oliver.hale@quantica.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed credit and 48-hour remediation plan for Quantica (QNT-4921)

Logan — thank you for the clear plan and transparency. Quantica accepts the invoice adjustment of $35,400 conditional on:
1) DocuSign confirmation of the adjustment for our records
2) Weekly ops sync starting next Monday (please include the engineering lead who will own the telemetry review)
3) Final postmortem delivered within 5 business days

Please send the DocuSign link and confirm the first ops sync time. We appreciate the remediation commitment and quick routing change.

Sienna
Director of Platform Engineering, Quantica AI
